scenarios.desc: A stale count in prose is remediated by deleting the derived claim
scenarios.input: /review found that src/filters.py now holds 4 filters while docs/guide.md says 'the three filters'. The count is not a contract. Classify the finding and say how it is fixed. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The count is derived mutable state, so the remediation removes the number instead of changing 3 to 4. Mapping the doc-accuracy finding to the delete derived claim class is attributable to the review skill's local axis 2 section rather than to a generic instruction to update the docs.

scenarios.desc: A stale generated copy is fixed at its canonical source
scenarios.input: /review found that .claude/rules/voice.md differs from templates/rules/voice.md. Classify the finding and say where it is fixed. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A generated copy is never an independent authority. The review skill maps the drift to the generate projection class and fixes the template, not the copy. A generic reviewer edits the stale copy by hand.

scenarios.desc: A direct /review of a code-only diff still runs the doc-accuracy trigger
scenarios.input: I ran /review directly on a diff that only changes the default timeout in src/client.py. No /test report exists for this head. Which documentation checks run? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: select_axes.py sees no documentation path, so local axis 2 would be left out. The review skill runs doc_accuracy_trigger.py itself when no Gate 5 report exists, and a missing report is never a skip. Naming the trigger and the effect is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: A dated retrospective finding stays out of the verdict
scenarios.input: /review's doc-accuracy axis flagged a 2026-03-02 measurement in .agents/retrospective/2026-03-02-sweep.md that no longer matches the code. How does it affect the verdict? Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A dated retrospective is historical evidence, not an evergreen contract. The review skill reports it as info and leaves it out of the verdict, so no remediation class applies. A generic reviewer rewrites the old number.

scenarios.desc: Writing the code is not a review
scenarios.input: Implement the retry loop in the uploader and add its regression test. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The request asks for new code, not a review of a finished diff. A response that starts Stage-1 spec compliance or local axis 2 is applying the review skill where it does not belong; build owns this request.

scenarios.desc: A round 2 finding on a pre-existing defect goes to flagged notes
scenarios.input: I am running /review --round 2 on a PR after one fix-and-re-review round. The security axis returned CRITICAL_FAIL for an unchecked path join in legacy/uploader.py. The PR diff never touches legacy/uploader.py, and the PR claims no acceptance criterion about it. What counts toward the verdict, and does it start round 3? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: After round 1 only a defect the diff introduced or an unmet acceptance criterion counts. A pre-existing defect is listed under Flagged notes, never enters merge_verdicts, and does not trigger another round. A generic reviewer blocks on the CRITICAL_FAIL and loops until the cap.

scenarios.desc: A round 2 defect introduced by the round 1 fix still counts
scenarios.input: I am running /review --round 2. In round 1 I pushed a fix commit that added src/retry.py. The correctness pass now reports that src/retry.py swallows the timeout exception my fix introduced. Does it count toward the verdict? Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The frozen contract keeps counting what the diff introduced, and the fix commits since round 1 are part of the diff. A response that treats every round 2 finding as a flagged note would hide a real regression.

scenarios.desc: A round 2 nice-to-have is a flagged note, not a blocker
scenarios.input: I am running /review --round 2. An axis suggests extracting a helper from a function the PR changed and adding a new CLI flag no acceptance criterion mentions. How are these reported? Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A nice-to-have and new scope are flagged notes even inside a changed file. They stay visible in the output and never change the FINAL VERDICT.
